headline: This law extends federal death and disability benefits to public safety officers and their survivors when COVID-19 causes death or injury.
what_it_does: The Public Safety Officers' Benefits Program normally pays benefits to officers and survivors when an officer is killed or hurt in the line of duty. This law adds a general presumption that an officer who dies from COVID-19 or related complications was injured in the line of duty. It also presumes that COVID-19 or related complications suffered by an officer count as a line-of-duty injury for disability benefits.

who_it_affects.group: Public safety officers, such as law enforcement officers
who_it_affects.how: Officers who become disabled by COVID-19 or related complications can be treated as having a line-of-duty injury for disability benefits.

who_it_affects.group: Survivors of public safety officers who die from COVID-19
who_it_affects.how: Eligible survivors, such as family members, can receive death benefits because the officer's COVID-19 death is presumed to be a line-of-duty death.

when_it_takes_effect: The law was enacted on August 14, 2020. The official summary does not state a separate effective date.
